simple.meaning: תָּעַע (tâʻaʻ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to cheat ; by analogy, to maltreat.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Genesis, 2 Chronicles, beginning at Genesis 27:12. The surrounding contexts include family, prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תָּעַע (H8591) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: תָּעַע (tâʻaʻ) / H8591 is traced through Genesis 27:12, 2 Chronicles 36:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to cheat ; by analogy, to maltreat
definitions.full: H8591. ta 'a' [ תָּעַע ] verb Pilpel, Hithpa`el mock (compare Arabic image unavailable stammer , also shake violently ; onomatopoetic); — Pilpel Participle מְתַעְתֵּ֑עַ Gen 27:12 +? a mocker. Hithpa`el Participle plural מִתַּעְתְּעִים 2Chr 36:16 , with ב person, mocking at his prophets (+ בּוֺזִים מַלְעִבִים, ).

occurrences.englishText: What if my father touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”
but they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets, until Yahweh’s wrath arose against his people, until there was no remedy.
